claim: In WebAIM's 2025 automated scan of one million home pages (human- and AI-built alike, not AI-specific), 79.1% had low-contrast text and 55.5% missing image alt text.
quote: WCAG Failure Type % of home pages Low contrast text 79.1% Missing alternative text for images
title: The WebAIM Million 2025

claim: In WebAIM's 2025 scan, 34.2% of form inputs on home pages (6.3 inputs per page on average) lacked a proper label.
quote: Home pages had 6.3 form inputs on average. 34.2% of those form inputs were not properly labeled
title: The WebAIM Million 2025

claim: In WebAIM's 2025 scan, home pages using ARIA averaged 57 detected errors against 27 for pages without ARIA; WebAIM says this does not necessarily mean ARIA caused them.
quote: Home pages with ARIA present had over twice as many errors (57 on average) than pages without ARIA (27 on average)
title: The WebAIM Million 2025

claim: NN/g states that well-designed empty states in applications can increase user confidence, improve learnability and help users start key tasks quickly.
quote: Well-designed empty states in applications can help increase user confidence, improve system learnability, and help users get started with key tasks quickly.
title: Empty States in Application Design: 3 Guidelines

claim: NN/g guidance says error messages must carry explanatory copy that helps the user recover and cannot rely on visuals alone.
quote: Error messages cannot rely on visuals alone. They must contain copy to elaborate and assist the user with recovering from the error.
title: Error-Message Guidelines

claim: NN/g observes that product teams focused on the ideal path treat deviations such as errors as a frustrating afterthought.
quote: Product teams can be so focused on designing or engineering the idealistic user path that deviations from that path become a frustrating afterthought.
title: Error-Message Guidelines

claim: Baymard reports, from repeated large-scale checkout testing, that the content of the error message is vital to users' ability to recover quickly from the error.
quote: the content of the error message itself is vital to user’s ability to quickly
title: Improve Validation Errors with Adaptive Messages

claim: Stanford Persuasive Technology Lab guidelines (2002, based on research with over 4,500 people) state that typographical errors and broken links hurt a site's credibility more than most people imagine.
quote: errors and broken links hurt a site's credibility more than most people imagine.
title: Stanford Guidelines for Web Credibility

claim: A 2026 blind survey of 92 participants rated AI-generated interface prototypes positively on pragmatic aspects (usability, efficiency) and neutral or negative on hedonic aspects (originality, innovation).
quote: Results indicate positive evaluations in pragmatic aspects, such as usability and efficiency, and neutral or negative evaluations in hedonic aspects, including originality and innovation.
title: Usable but Conventional: An Empirical Study on the UX of AI-Generated Interface Prototypes
